units.text: Every method in this chapter quietly assumed that the data is a table of independent rows that could be shuffled freely. Much valuable data is not. It arrives in time order, as a network, or as a list whose order is the whole point, and such data gets its own section later, once the machinery of deep learning is in place. That machinery is where we go next. Everything so far has depended on someone choosing good features to give the model; the next chapter is about models that learn to build their own. Its story begins with a newspaper headline from 1958, and with a promise that turned out to be wildly premature.

Going further. If you wondered how to choose thresholds like the deployment-risk cut-offs, section 10.3 takes that up, and if you wondered whether a model’s 0.83 can really be trusted as a probability, section 10.5 does. How a cause is told apart from something that merely moves along with it is the subject of section 11.1. And if you wondered what to do with data that arrives in time order, as a network or as a ranked list, section 8.3 takes it up.
